title: Corporate net-zero target and Jackson Avenue housing referral
subtitle: Also covered: a private street name on Otterbein Road and rezoning for a school expansion on Laurentian Drive.
overview: The committee recommended that Council endorse a 2050 net-zero target for the City's own operations, along with the second-generation Corporate Climate Action Plan. It also received the 2023 corporate emissions update for information {{vote:m2}}. Staff said the plan focuses on facilities and fleet, and that the cost and pace of progress depend on new technology and grants.

The most contested item was a proposal for about 118 stacked townhouse units on Jackson Avenue and Brentwood Avenue. After several residents spoke against it, the committee referred the application to the April 29 Council meeting {{vote:m4}}. That gives the applicant time to respond to concerns about building height, setbacks, emergency access, tenant displacement and parkland. No decision on the application was made.

The committee also recommended an official plan amendment and rezoning for 15 Laurentian Drive so a neighbouring Christian school can expand {{vote:m3}}. It supported the name Otterbein Crescent for a private street at 130 Otterbein Road {{vote:m1}}. Council will consider all of these recommendations later.

decisions.item: Corporate climate action plan and net-zero target
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council endorse a corporate 2050 net-zero target and the CorCAP 2.0 Pivot: Net-Zero plan, submit it to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities' Partners for Climate Protection Program, and received the 2023 emissions inventory update for information.

decisions.item: Jackson Avenue and Brentwood Avenue development
decisions.detail: The committee referred the staff recommendation on the official plan and zoning changes to the April 29 Council meeting, so the applicant can consider feedback on height, setbacks, emergency and waste vehicle access, hydrants, unit numbers, tenant displacement, rental replacement and parkland.

The committee recommended adopting the official plan amendment, for forwarding to the Region of Waterloo for approval, and approving the zoning change from low-rise residential to institutional for the Kitchener Waterloo Christian School Society.
The committee supported naming a private street in the development at 130 Otterbein Road "Otterbein Crescent" and directed Legal Services to advertise and prepare the required by-law.

debate: On the climate plan, one councillor questioned why embodied carbon and geothermal energy were not in the plan. Staff said embodied carbon will be reported on new builds and that a green building standard is expected to address geothermal and other renewables.

Councillors noted that the net-zero target depends on emerging technology, grants from senior governments and possibly debt. One said the City should still set an example, and another said they would support it knowing those drawbacks.

On Jackson Avenue, delegates opposed the proposed height, floor space ratio, setbacks and parking. They also raised traffic, tree loss, flooding on Montgomery Road, and a new roadway at 136 Brentwood Avenue that they considered unsafe. They said they were not opposed to development that follows the existing zoning.

Staff and the applicant's team said the site is already zoned for stacked townhouses and that the extra height raises basement units above grade. They said the second access was needed for servicing, traffic dispersal and fire access. Councillors asked about an emergency-only access, lower ceiling heights, keeping the brick fence and a rental replacement plan.

On Laurentian Drive, councillors asked what would happen to the tenants of the house to be demolished and asked for relocation assistance. Several said they would prefer a playground to a parking lot, while noting the school's role as a good neighbour.
